The verse establishes Maqabis-of-Moab as the principal protagonist of 2 Mq — beginning his arc at the moral nadir. His subsequent arc (chs. 2-4) is the LONGEST PORTRAIT of a Gentile convert to Mosaic religion in the entire Ethiopian biblical canon.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

'They made the corpses of your servants food for the birds of heaven. They made the flesh of your righteous ones food for the wild beasts of the desert' — DIRECT QUOTATION of Psalm 79:2-3 (LXX 78:2-3 'the dead bodies of your servants have they given to be food for the birds of the heaven, the flesh of your saints to the beasts of the earth') — a psalm sung specifically about the destruction of Jerusalem and the desecration of the Temple. The quotation locates the present narrative theologically in the post-586-BCE 'lament-over-Jerusalem' tradition, alongside Lamentations + Jeremiah's prophecies + Ezekiel's exile-oracles. Meqabyan's use of Ps 79 is a structural-citation: the psalm becomes the LITURGICAL FRAME for the 2 Mq destruction-narrative.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

Maqabis-of-Moab's COMPOSITE-GEOGRAPHIC PROVENANCE (vv. 1-3): 'in Syria, between the two rivers' — the Mesopotamian river-doublet (Tigris + Euphrates per Genesis 2:14 + Daniel 10:4) is ANACHRONISTICALLY paired with the Moabite-king identification, producing the characteristically Meqabyan COMPOSITE-HISTORICAL GEOGRAPHY (the same telescoping appears at 1 Mq 2:2 'land of the Chaldeans, in Midian, and in the country of the Medes' for the Maqabean homeland). Per Horovitz 1905 p. 195: the composite-geography is intentional — Meqabyan does not pretend to historical-precision but constructs a TYPOLOGICAL LANDSCAPE where each imperial-pride-locus collapses into the others. The verse establishes Maqabis-of-Moab's reach as Aramaic-Mesopotamian-and-Moabite — a SYNECDOCHIC FIGURE for Gentile-imperial-violence rather than a specific historical-king.

Maqabis-of-Moab's PRE-DESTRUCTION RAGE-FORMULA (vv. 6-9): the king's chest-beating + face-rending in fury at Jewish-resistance parallels the standard biblical TYRANT'S RAGE topos — Pharaoh at Exodus 14:5-7 (regret-and-pursuit); Sennacherib at 2 Kings 18:19-35 / Isaiah 36 (Rabshakeh's blasphemous-defiance); Nebuchadnezzar at Daniel 3:13 (wrath-on-three-young-men); Antiochus IV at 1 Maccabees 1:24 ('he took the spoils away in a great pride'). Meqabyan develops the rage-formula INTO PROVOCATIVE-PROVOCATION: the king's fury is not directed at military-strategic threats but at THE EXISTENCE-AS-SUCH of God's people — the rage is theological-ontological rather than political-strategic. Tewahedo homiletic tradition reads 1 Mq 1:6 alongside the parallel Pharaoh-rage pattern as a perennial-typology of the tyrant who hates God's people for what-they-are rather than what-they-do.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

DESTRUCTION-OF-JERUSALEM SEQUENCE (vv. 14-17): Maqabis-of-Moab's advance from the Jabbok river (Genesis 32:22 Jacob's wrestling-site) to the city-square of Jerusalem traces the ROUTE OF DIVINE-JUDGMENT-INVERTED: where Israel under Joshua + the Judges advanced from the Jabbok-eastern-Transjordan into the Land, Maqabis reverses the conquest-direction — Gentile-Moab now penetrates the promised-land. The reverse-conquest motif parallels the standard PROPHETIC INVERSION of conquest-narratives (Isaiah 10:5-11 — Assyria as God's rod-of-anger; Jeremiah 25:8-11 — Babylon as God's servant; Habakkuk 1:5-11 — the Chaldeans as God's terrible-instrument). Meqabyan's distinctive emphasis: the destruction is theologically-interpreted (the seed 1:10 Ps 79:2-3 quotation locates it within lament-tradition) rather than presented as raw-historical-tragedy. Sets up the prophet Re'ay's intervention at Ch 2.
